newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle break into close, feeders slip.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle break into close, feeders slip.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were lightly mixed much of the day but broke late as fund selling hit August. Feeder cattle also slipped to mixed levels as spillover from live cattle offset early support from lower corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.525 cent per lb lower to unchanged with June off 0.300 at 63.450 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.100 higher to 0.150 lower with only August up at 76.050 cents.
Live cattle held in a narrow trading range early before coming under local and fund selling pressure late. Sell stops were hit under 63.500 in August, traders said.
"Funds are big longs in cattle," one trader said.

Some pressure stemmed from expectations that cash markets will remain under pressure through the summer. There are more than adequate fed cattle supplies to meet demand despite the active feedlot movement last week which saw a record movement in Kansas, traders said.

"The showlist this week is down but it still indicates there are plenty of cattle out there," said Dave Maher from Securities Corporation of Iowa. "Just the mere fact the numbers are there is enough to keep the markets on the defensive."
The next Cattle-on-Feed report is expected to show continued larger than year-ago on-feed supplies.

Early analyst projections put total on-feed cattle supplies in the major seven-state area between 112 and 114 percent of a year ago as of June 1. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates ranged from 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings 97 to 100 percent.

Cargill Investor Services, Refco, Prudential Securities and ABN Chicogo Corp sold late. In live cattle options, commission houses sold August 65 and 66 calls, October 69 calls and August 62 puts, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures show strength much of the day following lower corn futures and a higher index, but also drifted back late on spillover weakness from live cattle futures, traders said.

Futures appeared due for a bounce after reaching six-week lows Friday, but the outlook for heavy fed cattle supplies through the summer may limit interest for replacement feeders even if feeder supplies are tight at times, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.28 at $77.76 per cwt, its highest level since August 19, 1994.
Locals and Rand Financials sold late after Refco, LIT division of First Options and ADM Investor Services bought August early, pit sources said.
